To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the change in lung volume ratio in AIS is affected by the severity of curve, rotation of apical vertebral body and kyphotic angle.

the ratio of convex lung volume to concave lung is higher in patients with AIS than in healthy controls and the ratio of convex and/or concave lung volume increases with increasing Cobb’s angle, rotation of apical vertebral body, and with decrease in kyphotic angle in patients with AIS.
the ratio of convex and the concave side lung volumes increases as the degree of curvature and rotation of the apical vertebra increases, and as the kyphotic angle decreases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of degree of curvature, degree of kyphosis/lordotic angle and rotation of apices on individual lung volume in adolescent patients with idiopathic scoliosisis.
the change of the ratio of convex and the concave lung volume and its relation with severity of scoliosis.
the effect of severity of scoliosis on lung volumes and its relationship with kyphosis, lordosis and apical vertebra rotation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in AIS, with increase in Cobb’s angle, the ratio of right to left lung volumes increases indicating the concave side lung volumes are comparatively more affected (i.e. decreased) than convex side volumes, which is further increased by the rotation of apical vertebral body, but decreased with decrease in kyphosis.
in AIS, the degree of curvature and rotation of apically involved vertebrae have a significant effect on lung volume and the effect is more prominent on the concave side.

with increase in degree and severity of scoliosis (i.e. Cobb’s angle, rotation and kyphosis), there is a decrease in concave side lung volumes and an increase in the ratio of convex side to concave side volume.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
with increase in the degree of curvature, rotation of apical segment and decrease in the angle kyphosis, there is a significant increase in the right to left lung ratio.
the degree of scoliotic curvature and apical rotation of the vertebrae have an effect on the ratio of convex and the concave lung volume.

with increasing severity of curve, and rotation of the apical vertebra in AIS, the concave side lung volumes decreases and the convex side lung volume increases, indicating the concave side of lung is more affected than the convex side.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with increase in the degree of curvature, the ratio of right to left lung volumes increases, i.e., the right lung is more affected than the left lung.
the degree of hypokyposis/lordosis and degree of rotation of apical vertebral body have an effect on the ratio of convex and the concave lung volume.

the ratio of lung volume in AIS patients with right thoracic curve is affected by severity of curve, kyphosis and axial rotation of apical vertebral body, and that the concave side lung is more affected than the convex side lung.
